newsitem.title: USA: Alumax sees strong growth in extrusions.
newsitem.headline: Alumax sees strong growth in extrusions.

text.p: Marc Czachorski, executive vice president of Alumax Transportation Products, said he expects to see double-digit annual growth in the U.S. aluminum extrusions market for bridges, streets and highways.

Speaking at the Aluminum Association's Alumitech conference here, Czachorski predicted continued strong growth in demand for aluminum extrusions for consumer durable goods such as air conditioners, freezers, and refrigerators, particularly as economic growth gathers pace across the developing world.

"A lot of money is going to be invested over the next 10 to 20 years in the infrastructure of the United States," he said, displaying figures which put 1996 extrusion shipments to the infrastruture market at 34 million pounds, versus 27 million pounds in 1991.
"We think this is an area that is going to grow at double-digit rates," he added.
Czachorski also said that extrusion shipments to the consumer durables market rose 58% last year.
"Aluminum has virtually taken over the market, and we expect this trend to continue as some of the developing countries raise their demand."
Alumax Transportation Products is a division of Alumax Inc
